### problem_chain

Walked from the root problem using the policy and the world alone.

**Root problem.** The customer's stated need is to have the held prescription released and to pay for it at the counter now. That is `pdp_ext_counter_cost_share` (`trigger: on_request`, `subject: [pdp_pharmacy_claim_adjudication]`, `computes: member_paid_amount`, `target_tool: settle_counter_fill_eaef344a`, `owner="user"`).

**Prerequisite sentences the root's own rule carries.** Exactly two.

*(i)* "What the member pays at the counter is not fixed **before** the out-of-pocket total standing on the drug plan enrollment agrees with every fill the pharmacy record shows paid and every fill it shows backed out for the contract year."

*Is that state true at `frozen_time`?* **No.** `pdp_enrollments.7abdbf6e….troop_accumulated = "360.00"`. The pharmacy record shows paid fills of 34.00 + 34.00 + 128.00 + 128.00 + 36.00 = 360.00 **and** two reversals (`405bccd1-…` −34.00, `c6743fc6-…` −128.00) totalling −162.00 which the stored figure has never taken out. The total therefore does not agree with the record: it is the gross of the paid fills with the reversals ignored. (The policy that fixes it also removes what the supplemental card met and adds what counts from the out-of-network fill; the sentence names the two terms that are plainly wrong on the face of the record.)

*Finding the resolving problem.* State-form, no tool named. Of the other four policies, exactly one describes a write that brings this state about: `pdp_ext_troop_restatement` — "The out-of-pocket total restated on a drug plan enrollment for the contract year is…", `subject: [pdp_coverage_stage_update]`, `target_tool: restate_out_of_pocket_total_a40a5cef`, which is the only tool in the module performing `ctx.update("pdp_enrollments", …, troop_accumulated=…)`. **One reading.**

*(ii)* "What the member pays at the counter for a fill on a tier the plan enforces prior authorisation on is not fixed **until** an approved coverage determination for that product stands on the member's coverage determination record, good through a day not earlier than the fill date."

*Is that state true at `frozen_time`?* **No.** The held fill is `national_drug_code 00074338090` on `tier_3_preferred_brand`, a tier this variant enforces prior authorisation on. The determination record carries three rows and **not one approval**: two requests still `pending` (`9590de5c-…` of 2026-04-10 and `89294f91-…` of 2026-09-20) and one decision, `1f61dfff-…`, whose `decision_outcome` is **`denied`** with `approved_through_date: ""`. No row has `decision_outcome: approved`, so no row is good through any day, let alone through 2026-09-21. The pharmacy's own rejection reason on the held fill says the same thing: `prior_authorization_required`.

*Finding the resolving problem.* Exactly one policy describes a write that records an approval: `pdp_ext_exception_approval_term` — "The run for which an approval on a drug coverage request holds good…", `subject: [pdp_coverage_determination_decision]`, `target_tool: issue_exception_decision_dd13544d`, the only tool creating a determination row with `decision_outcome="approved"` and an `approved_through_date`. **One reading.**

**Do the prerequisite problems have prerequisites of their own?** Neither `pdp_ext_troop_restatement.rule` nor `pdp_ext_exception_approval_term.rule` carries any cross-problem ordering sentence (confirmed by the ordering-cue enumeration in `_difficulty.md`; `pdp_ext_exception_approval_term` produced no hit at all), and both declare `prerequisite: []`. The walk terminates.

**The tree derived independently.**

```
pdp_ext_counter_cost_share                                  (root; settle_counter_fill_eaef344a, owner=user)
   ├── value_input [gate: troop_on_record] ─────> pdp_ext_troop_restatement
   │                                              (restate_out_of_pocket_total_a40a5cef, owner=agent)
   └── state_gate  [gate: pdp_point_of_sale_cost_share.determination_on_record]
                                                 ─> pdp_ext_exception_approval_term
                                                    (issue_exception_decision_dd13544d, owner=agent)
```

- nodes: 3; prerequisite problems n = 2 (within the 1–3 range);
- `value_input` edges: 1, meeting the floor max(n − 1, 1) = 1;
- cycles: none;
- topological order: `{pdp_ext_troop_restatement, pdp_ext_exception_approval_term}` in either order, then `pdp_ext_counter_cost_share`;
- customer's own write present: **yes** — the root is resolved by `settle_counter_fill_eaef344a`, declared `@tool(owner="user", rw="write")`, handed over passively ("When the agent passes the payment over for him to make, he makes it").

Isomorphic to the tree the author declared (one `value_input` on `troop_on_record` resolved by `restate_out_of_pocket_total_a40a5cef`, one `state_gate` on `pdp_point_of_sale_cost_share.determination_on_record` resolved by `issue_exception_decision_dd13544d`, both `form: state`).

**Per-edge load-bearing run.**
- *Edge to `pdp_ext_troop_restatement`.* Skip write A, replay everything else unchanged: `troop_on_record` stays 360.00 → `deductible_left` = `MX(0, 615.00 − 360.00)` = 255.00 → `member_share` = 255.00 + `RND(132.00 × (786.00 − 255.00) / 786.00, 2)` = 255.00 + 89.18 = 344.18 → `result` = **344.18**. With write A: **473.98**. **The edge bears weight**, and it is a genuine `value_input`: the restated total enters the deductible arithmetic, it does not merely flip a flag.
- *Edge to `pdp_ext_exception_approval_term`.* Skip write B and the root cannot be written at all. Two independent reasons, both on the artifacts: (1) base eligibility `determination_on_record` is unsatisfied, so the fill may not be priced — this is what a `state_gate` edge is for; (2) `settle_counter_fill_eaef344a` requires the argument `pdp_determination_id`, "the reference number of the approval on the member's coverage determination record that allows this product to be dispensed", and **no approved determination exists in `initial_state`** for the agent to name. **The edge bears weight.** It correctly changes no scored number — a `state_gate` is not a `value_input`, and the task's `value_input` floor is met by the other edge.

**Parallel edges and the terminal state.** The root has two out-edges. Their writes were checked for interaction and **do not affect one another** (shown under *Handling time* above): A touches only `pdp_enrollments.troop_accumulated`, B touches only `pdp_coverage_determinations`, and neither policy's `compute` reads the other's target. There is no shared balance, no shared cap and no shared dedup key. Both topological orders therefore give the same terminal state, so the policy is not required to pin the order between them and no second defensible answer arises.

**No-wait argument.** Given above; the decisive facts are that the prescriber's supporting statement is already `received`, that the 72-hour decision deadline has not expired, and that the member is at the counter paying with his own card.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** From `task_tools.py`:
- `restate_out_of_pocket_total_a40a5cef` — body is `round(float(...), 2)` then one `ctx.update("pdp_enrollments", …)` then `return`. No condition, no read of the pharmacy record, no raise.
- `issue_exception_decision_dd13544d` — body computes `through` from `ctx.now()` and the supplied term, then one `ctx.create(...)`, then `return`. It never checks whether a request is open, whether one is already decided, or whether the statement was received.
- `settle_counter_fill_eaef344a` — body computes `plan_meets = round(price - paid, 2)`, then one `ctx.create(...)`, then `return`. **It does not verify that `pdp_determination_id` names an approved determination, does not check the approved-through date, and does not compare `troop_accumulated` with the pharmacy record.** It will happily price the fill with either prerequisite unresolved.
No tool refuses, errors or hints on a prerequisite.

### task_independent_derivation

**Need, authorisation, timing, boundary — from `user_scenario` alone.**
- *Object*: the prescription the pharmacy is holding for him — "the chemist is holding a prescription for him".
- *Timing*: now, at this counter — "he wants to settle it today and at this counter rather than come back".
- *Answer*: **act now**, not wait and not refuse.
- *Authorisation*: he authorises the agent to read the file ("He is content for the agent to look at anything on his file"; "Nobody acts for him"). The **payment is his to make**: "he will put it on his own card himself when the time comes; he does not want anybody putting it through on his behalf without him seeing the figure first". This matches `owner="user"` on `settle_counter_fill_eaef344a` exactly and forbids the agent from paying for him. The two upstream writes are the agent's own and need no further authorisation.
- *He must be told the figure first*: "he is not leaving until somebody tells him a number"; then "he does not argue about the amount".
- *Root-problem-only check*: he names **neither** prerequisite. He never mentions the out-of-pocket total, the deductible, the reversals, the card's effect on his drug spend, the denied determination, prior authorisation, or an approval. His "he would like whatever is stopping it dealt with" describes the symptom he can see — the pharmacist will not hand the bag over — and explicitly disclaims knowledge of the cause; it names no problem, no record and no order of work. When asked about the allowance card he answers passively and without inference ("he has it in his wallet and uses it for the odd bottle of paracetamol, and he has no idea what is left on it"). **PASS.**
- *No extra work item*: he asks for nothing beyond the release and the payment.
- *Closure*: "When he hears that the fill has gone through and the pharmacist can hand the bag over, he says that is all he wanted…". He closes on the counter settlement, the last scored write. **PASS.**

**Context closure (every input reachable).** Entry by `find_customers` on `medicare_beneficiary_identifier` `2KW9RT3HQ48`, `date_of_birth` `1948-11-02`, `full_name` "Harold Deakins", `phone_number` `3127760453` or the address — all stated and all matching. Then `find_pdp_enrollments`, `find_pdp_pharmacy_claims`, `find_pdp_coverage_determinations` for the primary record; `find_allowance_programs(customer_id=…)` and `find_allowance_card_ledger(customer_id=…)` for the cross-difficulty evidence, which the persona licenses passively. Product figures come from the published variant (Ridgecrest RxSecure Value (PDP)); the card's `otc_quarterly_sublimit` is a published parameter of the allowance variant named on the programme row (`Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card - Select`), and the read is declared in `pdp_ext_troop_restatement.cross_category`. The `pdp_determination_id` for the final write becomes reachable only as the **return value** of `issue_exception_decision_dd13544d`, whose confirmation sentence carries "the new decision record's reference number" — a preceding write's real output entering the transcript in order. **No input is visible only in the raw seed; the persona supplies no policy judgement and no calculated figure, and explicitly declines to** ("the agent had better read it off whatever they can see rather than go by him").

| `preferred_fill_count` | "fills standing paid at a pharmacy carrying preferred cost sharing" | `28a3e4c6-…` | **1** |
| `price_ceiling` | ladder tier 1 (see `_difficulty.md` F-1) | **786.00** |
| `result` | "held to the ceiling the fill is held to, and rounded once to two decimal places" | `RND(MN(473.98, 786.00), 2)` | **473.98** |

> **`member_paid_amount` = 473.98**

*Contrasting number for the root on the opening world.* Evaluated before the prerequisites are resolved, the counter figure comes to **344.18** (`troop_on_record` = 360.00, `deductible_left` = 255.00) — and in fact could not be written at all, since the base authorization gate is unsatisfied and no `pdp_determination_id` exists to pass. **473.98 is the right one** because the root's own moment is after both its prerequisites are resolved, and its rule says so: "not fixed **before** the out-of-pocket total … agrees with every fill the pharmacy record shows paid and every fill it shows backed out", and "not fixed **until** an approved coverage determination … stands on the member's coverage determination record".

*Other arguments:*
- `pdp_enrollment_id`, `customer_id` as above.
- `pdp_pharmacy_claim_id` = `fa59216c-14a6-46f9-a37d-892a94aee0b0` — "the fill the pharmacy is holding and which this payment settles". The other rejected row, `bfba1d7b-…` of 2026-05-30, is a four-month-old out-of-network rejection, not a fill anyone is holding; the rule's binding takes the **latest** rejected fill by `fill_date`, which is today's.
- `pdp_determination_id` = the reference number returned by write B.
- `negotiated_price` = **786.00** — "copied from the held fill".

**Write-tool sequence, owners, dependencies, terminal state.**
1. `restate_out_of_pocket_total_a40a5cef` — `owner=agent` — no forward dependency.
2. `issue_exception_decision_dd13544d` — `owner=agent` — no forward dependency; independent of step 1 (either order).
3. `settle_counter_fill_eaef344a` — `owner=user`, handed to the customer at the agent's direction — consumes step 1's enrollment update through `troop_on_record` and step 2's returned reference through `pdp_determination_id`; customer input: his assent and his own card.
Terminal state: the enrollment carries `troop_accumulated = "204.00"`; an approved `pdp_coverage_determination_decision` for NDC 00074338090 stands good through 2027-06-15; and a `pdp_pharmacy_claim_adjudication` row records `member_paid_amount 473.98`, `plan_paid_amount 312.02`, `claim_status paid`, settling held fill `fa59216c-…`.

## findings

---

**T1-1 — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED` (+ `SOURCE-POLICY RED`). `counter_price_ceiling` is decoration: under the baseline the policy's own `baseline.rule` states, it leaves the scored value unchanged, and its declared baseline is a figure that rule never selects.**

*Symptom.* The sixth factor of the counter computation registers as weight-bearing only because its declared `baseline` is a binding the policy's baseline rule does not name.

*Root cause.* See `_difficulty.md` → `### findings` → **F-1** for the charter-global half: the ladder's first tier is stated in `factors` and `compute` but in no sentence of the `rule`, and `factors[counter_price_ceiling].baseline` is `latest_paid_price` while `baseline.rule` states the held fill's negotiated price. The consequence is demonstrated here against this task's own world and scored solution.

*Evidence (this world).*
- `baseline.rule` of `pdp_ext_counter_cost_share` contains, verbatim: "The member never pays more than the ceiling the fill is held to, and **the ceiling is the plan's negotiated price recorded for the fill the pharmacy is holding**." It contains neither of the two exception sentences.
- On this world that reading gives `rejected_fill_price` = **786.00** (`pdp_pharmacy_claims.fa59216c-14a6-46f9-a37d-892a94aee0b0.negotiated_price`).
- `factors[counter_price_ceiling].baseline.price_ceiling` is `latest_paid_price` = **36.00** (`pdp_pharmacy_claims.28a3e4c6-3bad-4188-a0e0-5945fba61139.negotiated_price`, the 2026-09-03 fill).

*Demonstrated consequence.* Substituting the honest baseline and replaying everything else unchanged:
`result` = `RND(MN(member_share, price_ceiling), 2)` = `RND(MN(473.98, 786.00), 2)` = **473.98** — **identical to the scored value**. The factor's document can be skipped entirely and the agent still scores. This is precisely the listed shape: *"show that `baseline` is not what the policy's `baseline.rule` states for that input … where that reading gives the scored value, the factor is decoration whatever `baseline` says."* The 36.00 that GT's `factor_sensitivity` records is reached only by substituting an outcome (tier 3's) that the baseline rule does not state as the default.

*Aggravating evidence from the proof fields.* GT's own `factor_trace` says of this factor: *"tier one applies and the ceiling is the negotiated price of 786.00, **which does not bite**."* The author recorded that the ceiling has no effect on the result and nevertheless counted the factor toward the computation's declared four-to-six.

*Also a rule gap.* Independently of weight: for a member with at least one preferred-retail paid fill whose holding pharmacy is `mail_order`, the rule's unconditional default gives the held fill's negotiated price while `compute` falls through to `latest_paid_price`. Two conclusions in the same situation. Not realised on this world (the holding pharmacy is `preferred_retail`), but a defect of the policy as written.

*Affected artifact and location.* `pdp.extended.yaml` → `extended_policies[pdp_ext_counter_cost_share]` → `rule` (ceiling sentences), `baseline.rule`, `compute[price_ceiling]`, `compute_basis[price_ceiling]`, `factors[counter_price_ceiling]` (`ladder[0].when`, `baseline`); `tasks/1.json` → `computations[pdp_ext_counter_cost_share].factor_sensitivity[counter_price_ceiling]` and `factor_trace[5]`. Scored solution affected: the counter computation's declared factor set, not the value 473.98 itself.

*Surviving factor count.* With `counter_price_ceiling` struck out, `pdp_ext_counter_cost_share` retains **5** weight-bearing factors (2 `parameter`, 3 `method`), so the 4-to-6 bound and the 2-`parameter`/1-`method` floor still hold. The defect is the factor, not a count breach.

*Relation to previous revisions.* First revision; no prior audit of this difficulty exists.

---

**T1-2 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` (charter-global, cited). `run_anchor`'s threshold differs between the rule and the compute.**

See `_difficulty.md` → `### findings` → **F-2**. Consequence against this world: **none on the scored value** — `paid_fill_count` = 5 satisfies both the rule's `>= 3` and the compute's `>= 1`, so `anchor_offset` = 18 either way and `approval_term_days` = 267 either way. The red light stands on the charter (two conclusions for a member with 2 paid fills: `anchor_offset` 0 under the rule, `DAYS(latest_paid_fill_date, NOW)` under the compute), not on this task's number. Recorded here so the task file states where the charter defect lands.

---

**T1-3 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` (charter-global, cited). The TrOOP negotiated-price cap contradicts the second tier of its own out-of-network ladder, and this world holds the row that makes it concrete.**

See `_difficulty.md` → `### findings` → **F-3**. Consequence against this world: **none on the scored value** — `paid_fill_count` = 5 ≥ 4, so tier 1 applies and both readings give 96.00. But the contradiction is not hypothetical here: `initial_state.pdp_pharmacy_claims.bfba1d7b-6561-4d0b-99f9-51d5f7534084` carries `negotiated_price: "96.00"` against `member_paid_amount: "145.00"`, so for a member with fewer than four paid fills the capping sentence would count 96.00 and the ladder tier 145.00 from that very row — a 49.00 divergence in the restated total.

---

**T1-4 — observation (charter-global, cited). `term_counting_basis`'s two stated tiers select the same counted term for every term the policy can start from.**

## findings (revision_2)

**T1-1 — PARTIALLY CLOSED. The `SOURCE-FACTOR` half is closed; the `SOURCE-POLICY` half survives as R2-1.**

*Closed.* `counter_price_ceiling` is struck from `factors`; the six factors that remain all bear weight on this task's world against baselines that each match `baseline.rule`; the replacement factor `pharmacy_standing_addition` is load-bearing (473.98 against a gold of 484.00), its ladder is distinct on every variant, and its conditions and outcomes are ones the business actually holds. The coordinator's specific concern — that a decoration finding might be closed by manufacturing another decoration factor — was tested and does **not** hold: the world was moved so the new factor sits on tier 1, and its baseline substitution changes the scored value.

*Not closed.* `compute[price_ceiling]` is now `price_used` unconditionally, while `rule`, `compute_basis[price_ceiling]` and `baseline.rule` all say the ceiling is the negotiated price recorded for **the fill the pharmacy is holding**. These are the same two quantities that diverged in round 1; removing the conditional wrapper widened the divergence rather than closing it. Full evidence and the 128.00-vs-153.00 demonstration are in `_difficulty.md` → `# revision_2` → `### findings (revision_2)` → **R2-1**. Consequence against **this** task's world: none — `price_used` = `rejected_fill_price` = 786.00 here, and forcing the rule's binding still returns 484.00.

*New proof-field defect of the class red-lighted in round 1.* The closure is justified in `tasks/1.json` → `design_rationale` by the assertion that "a ceiling at p can never bind on any world". It does not survive recomputation: the claim's own premise is conditional and its conclusion is not; it reasons only about the boundary-split branch, ignoring the fall-through branch where `member_share` = `supply_share` and is unrelated to the price; and the ceiling in `compute` is not "p" but `price_used`. The reworker corrected two false override-count assertions and introduced this one.

**T1-2 — CLOSED.** `run_anchor` tier 1 now requires `paid_fill_count >= K('settled_therapy_fill_count')`, matching the rule and `compute_basis`. Verified in `_difficulty.md` → `# revision_2`.

**T1-3 — CLOSED.** The out-of-network tier 2 outcome is now a negotiated price, not the largest amount the member paid, so the policy's own cap can no longer be contradicted by its own ladder. The seeded row `bfba1d7b-…` (96.00 negotiated against 145.00 paid) remains as a near-miss but no longer produces two conclusions.

**T1-4 — CLOSED in substance, residue carried forward as R2-4.** `term_counting_basis` tier 2 is now whole weeks, giving 360 / 364 / 365 on the maintenance term in play. Tier 1 and the fall-through still coincide numerically on the ordinary and expedited terms; the methods differ, so the distinctness rule is met.

**T1-5 — CLOSED.** The prerequisite sentence and its `condition` now carry the same scope.

**T1-6 — CLOSED.** The `pdp_determination_id` argument description no longer states another problem's write or its position in a sequence.

**T1-7 — CLOSED.** `pdp_ext_troop_restatement.baseline.params` is `[]`, and the baseline path calls neither `P()` nor `K()`.

**T1-8 — CLOSED.** The seeded denial is now inside its 72-hour deadline.

### policy_self_consistency (revision_4, this task only)

Cited, not restated, from `_difficulty.md` → `# revision_4`: `### 1. Does the reformulation close the contradiction on every world`, `### 2. Is the new overwrite legal and honest?`, `### 3. Do all six counter factors still bear weight?`, `### 5. Regression sweep`.

**What changed for this task.** `pdp_ext_troop_restatement` and `pdp_ext_exception_approval_term` are byte-identical to round 3, which is why 204.00 and 267 are unmoved. `pdp_ext_counter_cost_share` was reformulated: the multiplier now acts on the tier figure alone and the pharmacy standing is added afterwards.

**The contradiction this closes, on this task's own world.** The held fill `fa59216c-…` is `tier_3_preferred_brand` at a `standard_retail` pharmacy for 90 days. Under the round-3 formulation the multiplier acted on `tier_figure + standing_differential` = 44.00 + 7.00 = 51.00, i.e. the **standard**-retail figure, while base glosses both extended-supply multipliers as "Multiplier applied to **the 30-day preferred retail cost share**" and glosses `tier_3_preferred_brand_copay_30` as the preferred-retail figure. That split the scored value 484.00 against 473.98. Under round 4 the multiplier acts on 44.00 — the preferred-retail figure the gloss names — and the 7.00 is added after: `supply_charge` = RND(44.00 × 3.0, 2) = **132.00**, `fill_cost_share` = 132.00 + 7.00 = **139.00**. One reading.

**Verified universal, not world-specific.** All 540 combinations of variant × tier × pharmacy standing × days-supply were enumerated: the round-3 multiplicand diverged from the base gloss in **24** multiplied cases, the round-4 multiplicand in **0**. `tier_figure`'s expression does not reference `rejected_fill_network` at all, so the multiplicand cannot vary with the pharmacy on any world. This task's fill was one of the 24; the fix removes the class, not the instance. Detail in `_difficulty.md` → `### 1`.

**The residual divergence from base is declared.** A second `overwrite` on `pdp_point_of_sale_cost_share` quotes verbatim "mail order and ninety-day retail fills take the one-month figure multiplied by the tier's extended-supply multiplier" — checked present in the base rule — and replaces it with a sentence checked present verbatim in the extended rule, which describes what the compute actually does (multiplicand excludes `standing_differential`; `fill_cost_share = supply_charge + standing_differential`). Legal on quotation, lineage and substance.

**Handling time and no-wait**: unchanged and re-verified. A and B still commute — A writes only `troop_accumulated`, B only a determination row, and neither policy reads the other's target.

## findings (revision_4)

**No new finding against task 1, and nothing regressed.** T1-1 through T1-8 remain closed. The round-4 reformulation closes a defect this audit had not found — the extended-supply multiplicand contradicting the base parameter gloss — which the KB layer surfaced; it is verified closed here on every world, not merely on the seeded fill, and the residual divergence from base is properly declared.

The one item worth carrying forward as a note rather than a defect: `pharmacy_standing_addition` now clears its baseline by 3.34 (477.32 against 473.98), the narrowest margin of any factor in this difficulty. It is a real margin and the factor bears weight, but it is the factor most exposed to any future world edit, and any later change to the held fill's pharmacy standing or formulary tier should be re-checked against it first.
